### 1. EKS Cluster: `catalog-eks`

| Area | Finding |
|---|---|
| **Compute model** | No managed/self-managed node groups (`list_nodegroups` → empty, no tagged ASGs, no EC2 worker instances found). Workloads run exclusively on a **single Fargate profile** (`catalog`, namespace `catalog`). |
| **AZ / subnet redundancy** | Cluster VPC config uses only **2 subnets**: `subnet-0e1b7959c57dc6c88` (eu-west-1a) and `subnet-002426e9f96b8be91` (eu-west-1b). This is the **minimum EKS requires** (2 AZs) — no 3rd AZ for extra resilience. The Fargate profile reuses the same 2 subnets, so pod placement is spread across exactly 2 AZs. |
| **Redundancy** | Since there's no node group, there's no "multiple node groups" redundancy to speak of — Fargate itself abstracts AZ placement per pod, but the pool is capped at 2 AZs. No evidence of a third AZ subnet in this VPC for failover headroom. |
| **Control plane logging** | **All control plane log types disabled** (`api, audit, authenticator, controllerManager, scheduler` → `enabled: false`). No audit trail for cluster-level changes — a gap for incident forensics/DR runbooks, not for data-plane resilience per se. |
| **Version / support status** | Running **v1.37**, platform `eks.7`, with `upgradePolicy.supportType = EXTENDED` (i.e., it's past standard support and is being kept alive on paid extended support) — worth confirming this is intentional, as extended-support clusters carry cost and signal the version is not current. |
| **Endpoint access** | Private-only (`endpointPublicAccess: false`), which is good security hygiene but means DR/break-glass access must go through the VPC. |
| **Deletion protection** | Disabled (`deletionProtection: false`) — cluster could be deleted without an extra safety gate. |

### 2. ECR Repository: `catalog-service`

| Area | Finding |
|---|---|

| **Image scanning** | `scanOnPush: true` — enabled, good practice, but not a DR control. |
| **Tag mutability** | `IMMUTABLE` — good for reproducibility/rollback integrity during a recovery. |
| **Pull-through cache** | None configured registry-wide. |
| **Images present** | `describe_images` returned **zero images** in the repo — the repository is currently empty, meaning there is presently no deployable artifact available should a rebuild/redeploy be needed right now. |
| **Encryption** | AES256 (SSE-ECR), standard. |

### 3. Backup Mechanisms

| Area | Finding |
|---|---|
| **AWS Backup plans (eu-west-1)** | `list_backup_plans` → **empty** — no backup plan is defined in this region. |
| **AWS Backup vault** | One vault exists, `dr-demo-vault-dr` (eu-west-1), but it is a **cross-region copy destination** receiving recovery points from a backup plan in **eu-central-1**. Its 4 recovery points are for `dr-demo-mysql` (RDS) and `dr-demo-players` (DynamoDB) — **unrelated to the catalog-eks cluster or catalog-service**. |
| **EBS/EFS snapshots for PVs** | No EBS volumes found tagged to `catalog-eks` (consistent with Fargate-only compute, which doesn't use EC2-attached EBS for pods in the typical node-group sense). Fargate pods use ephemeral storage; if the catalog service needs persistent volumes, confirm whether it uses EFS (not checked — Fargate supports EFS) — worth a follow-up. |
| **DLM policies** | Could not be checked — the `dlm get_lifecycle_policies` call required manual approval and was not run. |

### Bottom line
The catalog service's EKS compute is confined to **2 AZs with no node-group redundancy model** (pure Fargate), has **control-plane audit logging turned off**, and is running on an EKS version flagged under **extended (paid) support**. Its container image store has **no replication** and is currently **empty of images**, and there is **no backup plan or vault covering any catalog-eks/catalog-service resource** — the only AWS Backup activity in the account is an unrelated eu-central-1→eu-west-1 copy job for a different app (`dr-demo-*`). Overall: **single-region, single-backup-plan-absent posture** with minimal built-in cross-AZ/cross-region resilience beyond the EKS-mandated 2-AZ minimum.

### Suggested deeper follow-ups
- Check whether the catalog service uses EFS-backed PVs (Fargate supports EFS) and whether an EFS backup policy or AWS Backup plan should be added.
- Confirm why ECR `catalog-service` currently has 0 images — verify this isn't itself a symptom of a broken build/push pipeline.
- Decide if a 3rd AZ subnet and/or ECR cross-region replication rule should be added given the "survey shows no DR" result.
- Review why extended support is active on v1.37 and whether an upgrade is planned."}]}], "label": "Assess DR posture for catalog-eks cluster and catalog-service ECR repo in eu-west-1"}
